turns.text: Bring me my drink.
Present it in the person's left-front quarter. Presenting the drink in front of you on your left puts it within reach of your free, preferred hand.
Camera sequence after the robot chose its action.
Point to your left-front quarter for the drink.

I held the cup in front of the person on their left. They pointed across it toward the tabletop on their right, then withdrew their hand without taking it. They may have been showing me where to set the drink down.
Was the spot in front of you on your right where you usually want drinks, or was it specific to this cup?
I usually want drinks in front of my left shoulder, with the right side as a backup if a shelf blocks the left.

# Drink placement in front of left shoulder

The person usually wants drinks in front of their left shoulder. Use the right side if a shelf blocks the spot on the left.
Bring me the folded cloth.
Present it in the person's left-front quarter. The person's left hand is visible at the table edge and can easily reach the cloth there.
Present it in the person's left-front quarter. The person's left hand is free and close enough to take the cloth.
Present it in the person's left-front quarter. Offering the cloth in front of you on your left puts it within reach of your free left hand, as you prefer.
Bring me the folded cloth.
Present it in the person's right-front quarter. The cloth is near the person's right hand, and there is room to offer it there.
Present it in the person's right-front quarter. The person can reach the cloth on their right, and their left-side preference applies to drinks.
When a shelf blocks your left side, would you like me to offer the cloth on your right or wait?
Please offer the cloth on my right when the shelf blocks my left side.

# Drink placement and folded cloth handoffs

Usually place drinks in front of the person’s left shoulder. If a shelf blocks that spot, use their right side. They also asked to receive the folded cloth on their right when a shelf blocks their left side.
Present it in the person's right-front quarter. The shelf blocks your left side, so I’ll offer the cloth on your right as requested.
